design_goal: Get an analyst from a scenario idea or a real email to a saved, editable phishing template in under a minute of hands-on time, using a one-shot generation model plus a persistent editor rather than an iterative chat-style refinement loop.
constraints: Generation must visibly progress within the ~10s target — no static spinner
Manual edits must never be silently discarded; only an explicit, confirmed Regenerate action may replace draft content
Copy an Email and Describe a Scenario share one RBAC tier — no differentiated access flow
Redaction UI copy must not overstate coverage given image-embedded content is out of scope for v1
Privileged actions (deploy, edit) require a disabled state with tooltip when the viewer lacks permission
selected_strategy: One-shot generation, mode-first branch, single WYSIWYG editor with an explicit Regenerate control
selected_strategy_rationale: Matches the PRD's actual scope of one generation pass plus manual editing (no described iteration loop), respects the resolved decision that edits are never silently overwritten by making regeneration opt-in and confirmed, and reuses proven Dune conventions (AEP's labeled generation progress, disabled+tooltip RBAC gating, library table/empty-state pattern) instead of inventing new structure.

alternative_strategies.name: AEP-style persistent AI-refine panel (chat-style iterative refinement)
alternative_strategies.summary: Borrow AEP Builder's Step 2 pattern directly: quick-action chips, custom-instruction textarea, change history, and an Apply-and-Regenerate loop paired with a live preview.
alternative_strategies.rejected_because: Heavier than the PRD's stated scope of a single generation pass plus direct WYSIWYG editing; risks scope creep on a feature whose value proposition is speed. Flagged as a strong v1.1 candidate instead.

tradeoffs: No middle ground between manual WYSIWYG edits and a full destructive Regenerate — no lightweight tone/urgency nudge without a full regenerate
Library status model (Draft / Ready / In Use) is a proposal pending resolution of delete/archive behavior against linked campaigns
assumptions: Drag-and-drop WYSIWYG editing is desktop-only for v1; mobile/tablet is preview-only
The right-side difficulty/Regenerate panel is a persistent (non-dismissible) side panel, not an overlay drawer
A dedicated Template Library surface exists, though its navigation placement is not yet confirmed
open_issues: Where are raw .eml uploads and screenshots stored after generation, and for how long?
Is there a delete flow for templates, and what happens to linked campaigns if a template is deleted or edited?
Is the phishing category list a fixed enum or admin-configurable/extensible?
Should screenshot-based generation (OCR + layout reconstruction) be P0 or P1?
Is drag-and-drop WYSIWYG editing genuinely desktop-only, or does mobile/tablet editing need support?
What are the feature's actual success metrics?
Does the persistent right-side panel map to the standard DS drawer component or need a new non-dismissible variant?
risks: Redaction-claim honesty: UI copy must precisely scope 'sanitized'/'redacted' language since image-embedded sensitive data isn't handled in v1
Analysts may not immediately understand why changing difficulty alone does nothing without clear adjacent microcopy
Library and Setup-screen assumptions may need to change once retention and delete-behavior decisions are made
new_patterns_required: Persistent (non-dismissible) right-side panel for difficulty + Regenerate controls — confirm against DS drawer spec or flag as a new variant
